definition: A training schedule technique that gradually increases the learning rate from a small value at the start of training before transitioning to the main schedule.
details: Learning rate warmup helps stabilize training in the early stages, particularly for large transformer models, where using the full target learning rate immediately can lead to instability or divergence.
story: Imagine teaching a friend to shoot a basketball. They miss, and you walk them backwards through the shot — elbow, wrist, release — to find what needs fixing. Think of it this way: A training schedule technique that gradually increases the learning rate from a small value at the start of training before transitioning to the main schedule. And here is the clever part: Learning rate warmup helps stabilize training in the early stages, particularly for large transformer models, where using the full target learning rate immediately can lead to instability or divergence. It is learning from every miss instead of repeating the same mistake. And that is Warmup (learning rate) — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
